items.title: 68087_Cliff Leeman oral history interview
items.q: Tommy hired Walter Gross, a most brave pianist of many accomplishments, to play the piano for us.

ctx.x: that pot for the band, call it a day with your cooking! That was the end of our culinary exploits for the present, and Charlie had somebody come in and build a very special crate and box so he could carry the equipment on the road with him, which he did. And he has his own kitchen from then on, and I heard many stories about his efforts as a chef.

To keep These incidents -- in a musical context, I might add that during our show at the Capitol Theatre, I think we were the first jazz band -- I'm quite sure -- to do the Rhapsody in Blue in its entirety, which is quite a feat, and Tommy at that time had made records using large string sections, and to keep this picture and some of the arrangements which we played -- I don't know who talked him into it, but he had 20 girl violinists -- a string section with 20 girls, a complete string ensemble, among other…
